label: Point 7.5 cm (Small Holes)
note: Owner-uploaded reference images. Authoritative for construction/appearance; NOT usable as the tech-pack illustration (not line art, or shows multiple options).

references.evidence: Two-panel composite on white ground: LEFT is clean line art of a point collar with a horizontal collar bar/pin passing through one small eyelet in each collar point, the two points drawn nipped together under where the knot sits; RIGHT is a photographic/rendered white shirt front showing the same point collar with a straight collar bar and two visible ball-end studs seated in pinholes on each point, top button area open, one placket button below. Both panels show the feature the label names (point collar prepared with small pinholes for a collar pin).

Real photograph, tight chest crop: white point collar over a blue-striped shirt body, a barbell-style collar pin with two polished ball ends visibly threaded through a small hole in each collar point, sitting directly beneath a navy knit tie knot which is visibly arched forward by the pin. Grey herringbone jacket lapel at frame left. This is exactly the pin-collar mechanic the description states (pin nips the points together and arches the tie).

Real photograph of a white textured (pique/oxford) shirt collar on a form, no tie, neck open. A collar bar is threaded through a small eyelet in each collar leaf with a rectangular closure at centre, so the pinhole preparation is unmistakable. However the collar leaf tips read as soft/rounded rather than a crisp point at this resolution, so the shape may be a club/round pin collar rather than the point collar the label names.

Extreme close-up photograph of a white shirt collar: a straight metal collar bar with two dark gunmetal barbell ends threaded through one small eyelet in each collar point, points drawn together over the placket, collar edge topstitching and one button visible. The eyelet-and-bar preparation named by the label dominates the frame.
